english: Let $a,b,c$ be the roots of the equation $t^{3}-3t^{2}+1=0$, and let $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b&c\\b&c&a\\c&a&b\end{pmatrix}$. Then $\det\left(\mathrm{adj}\,A\right)+\det A$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $a,b,c$ समीकरण $t^{3}-3t^{2}+1=0$ के मूल हैं, तथा $A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b&c\\b&c&a\\c&a&b\end{pmatrix}$ है। तब $\det\left(\mathrm{adj}\,A\right)+\det A$ बराबर है
solution: For a $3\times3$ matrix $\det(\mathrm{adj}\,A)=(\det A)^{2}=729$ (positive, whatever the sign of $\det A$)
solution_full: Apply $C_1\to C_1+C_2+C_3$; every entry of the new first column is $a+b+c$, so $\det A=(a+b+c)\begin{vmatrix}1&b&c\\1&c&a\\1&a&b\end{vmatrix}$.
Apply $R_2\to R_2-R_1$ and $R_3\to R_3-R_1$: the determinant becomes $\begin{vmatrix}1&b&c\\0&c-b&a-c\\0&a-b&b-c\end{vmatrix}=(c-b)(b-c)-(a-c)(a-b)$.
So $\det A=-(a+b+c)\left(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}-ab-bc-ca\right)=-\left(a^{3}+b^{3}+c^{3}-3abc\right)$; this is symmetric in $a,b,c$, so the order of the roots does not matter.
For an $n\times n$ matrix, $A\,\mathrm{adj}\,A=(\det A)I$ gives $\det A\cdot\det(\mathrm{adj}\,A)=(\det A)^{n}$, so $\det(\mathrm{adj}\,A)=(\det A)^{n-1}$ when $\det A\neq0$.
originality_note: New: the entries of the cyclic determinant are the roots of a given cubic, so the value comes from Vieta (with ab + bc + ca = 0), and the adjugate step turns the negative determinant into a positive square (way 5). Closest known: evaluating |a b c; b c a; c a b| for given a, b, c, and det(adj A) = (det A)^2. Different because: a, b, c are irrational roots, so the property-based factorisation is forced, and the sign of det A decides between 702 and 756.

concept_use.Adjoint of a square matrix: det(adj A) = (det A)^{n-1} = (det A)^2 for the 3 x 3 matrix A.
concept_use.Application of properties of determinant: The column operation C1 -> C1 + C2 + C3 and row subtractions factor det A as -(a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca).

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: with the three numerical roots (40 digits) det A = -27.000 and det(adj A) = 729.000; the expression is symmetric in a, b, c so the order of roots is irrelevant. Changed: No change.
key_step: Factoring the cyclic determinant by properties and using Vieta with ab+bc+ca = 0, then det(adj A) = (det A)^2.
justification: Two ideas linked (determinant properties with Vieta, and the adjugate determinant rule) with a sign trap; comparable to the root-based evaluation in 2026-P1-Q13 (L3) and the matrix identities of 2021-P1-Q14 (L3).
